slides.title: The AI-Staffed IT Department
slides.subtitle: Readiness & 90-Day Pilot Proposal — Group IT Briefing
slides.notes: OPENING (memorize): 'Thank you for the time. In the next fifteen minutes I will show how we turn scattered AI usage into a governed, measurable capability in ninety days - and ask for one decision at the end.' Pause two seconds. Time: 1 min.

slides.title: Scattered AI tools today; one governed capability in 90 days

bullets.text: Where we are: strong delivery discipline; AI tools appearing ad-hoc across teams without coordination or measured value
What is changing: AI adoption is fragmenting - shadow tools, ungoverned data use, value that no one can prove
The answer: stand up an AI-staffed IT department as a 90-day pilot - six functions, gated pilots, measured value
The ask today: approve the 90-day pilot and its governance gates

slides.notes: MESSAGE: The whole argument in 30 seconds - executives can stop here and decide. Transition: 'Let me show why this is urgent, not just interesting.' Time: 2 min. If the slot shrinks, this slide alone carries the meeting.

slides.title: AI usage is growing faster than our ability to govern it
slides.subtitle: Left: where we stand. Right: what it costs to leave it scattered.

bullets.text: Where we are
IT delivery is disciplined and trusted
Teams already use AI tools ad-hoc (assistants, code helpers, reporting)
No common standards: no gate, no owner, no measured value
What scattered adoption costs
Shadow tools: unknown data handling - a governance exposure
Duplicated spend on overlapping tools
Real value stays anecdotal - cannot be scaled or defended

slides.notes: MESSAGE: The complication in the room's own language: risk + waste + unprovable value. Transition: 'The opportunity is not more tools - it is organizing the ones that matter.' Time: 2.5 min. Do not name specific tools or teams - keep it systemic, non-accusatory.

slides.title: The opportunity: a scored use-case portfolio, not a tool list

rows: High value, high confidence, human-final checks
Status reporting, meeting summaries, ticket triage
Code review assist, document drafting, analysis
Extended review checklist + user feedback loop
Agentic workflows for PMO data, AI ops reports
Kill or graduate at 90 days - no extensions

slides.notes: MESSAGE: Portfolio discipline replaces tool enthusiasm - every use case has a lane, an owner, and a gate. Transition: 'Here is the team structure that runs this portfolio.' Time: 2.5 min. Every example is drawn from work this department already does daily - nothing speculative.

slides.title: The operating model: six functions staffed by AI agents, led as a real team

rows: Solution design aligned to business goals

slides.notes: MESSAGE: This is a department, not a chatbot collection - the structure mirrors how real IT teams are organized. Transition: 'Autonomy is earned, not granted - here is the ladder.' Time: 2.5 min. This mirrors the six-pillar model already communicated publicly - consistency is deliberate.

slides.title: Autonomy is earned in steps, with gates at every stage

bullets.text: Every irreversible action passes a human gate - always
Red lines from day one: no autonomous spend, no autonomous messages on our behalf, no production changes without approval
Autonomy levels are documented, revocable, and logged

slides.notes: MESSAGE: Governance is the enabler, not the brake - this is what makes the pilot safe to approve. Transition: 'And here is the tier model that makes governance proportionate.' Time: 2 min. If asked about data safety: data-flow map exists per system before deployment - nothing enters prompts without classification.

slides.title: Three risk tiers, proportionate controls - aligned with group IT policy

rows: Internal drafts, summaries, no personal data
Review before launch, eval pass, named owner
Security review, data assessment, human approval gate, incident runbook

bullets.text: Every system: owner, tier, gate status, review date - auditable in 5 minutes

slides.notes: MESSAGE: Nothing ships outside proportionate governance - the audit trail already exists as a working procedure. Transition: 'What we will actually do in the first 90 days.' Time: 2 min. Aligned with existing group IT risk policy - this skill stack was built around it.

slides.title: The 90-day plan: three phases, each ending at a decision gate

bullets.text: Foundation (0-30): baseline measurement, use-case scoring, agent setup, governance pack signed
Gated pilots (31-60): 2-3 use cases live (status reporting, meeting intelligence, ticket triage) with weekly value tracking
Review & decision (61-90): measured results vs baseline; scale/adjust/stop recommendation to leadership

slides.notes: MESSAGE: Timeboxed with kill criteria - leadership gets a real decision point at day 90, not a fait accompli. Transition: 'What it costs - and what it returns, stated honestly.' Time: 2.5 min. Kill criteria are pre-agreed: no measured value by day 90 = stop, with lessons documented.

slides.title: Investment is mostly reallocated time; value is measured, not promised

rows: Market range for team AI tooling - to be confirmed in sourcing
From current reporting/support workload, not new headcount
Target 30-50% time reduction on pilot workflows
ASSUMPTION - baseline measured in weeks 1-2; ranges, not promises

bullets.text: All figures are estimates with stated assumptions; the pilot's first act is measuring the real baseline

slides.notes: MESSAGE: Honest numbers - small incremental cost, reallocated effort, and value stated as ranges with the baseline measured first. Transition: 'The risks, and who owns each one.' Time: 2.5 min. Do NOT oversell here - this slide's honesty is its persuasiveness. If challenged on ROI: 'That is exactly why the baseline is measured before anything scales.'

slides.title: Top risks have named owners and mitigations before day one

rows: Tier gates + data-flow maps before any deployment
Baseline measured first; value ledger reviewed weekly
Assist-first adoption; staff time reallocated, not added
Sanctioned path made easier than workaround; quarterly inventory

slides.notes: MESSAGE: We have thought about what can go wrong - and who owns each response. Transition: 'Which brings us to the decision.' Time: 1.5 min.

slides.title: The ask

bullets.text: Approve the 90-day AI department pilot
With its three governance gates and the day-90 decision point
Decision requested today: GO / ADJUST / NO-GO

slides.notes: CLOSING (memorize): 'We are asking for one decision today: approve the 90-day pilot with its governance gates. If the measured value is not there at day 90, we stop and we will have lost little. If it is there, we scale a capability our competitors are already building.' Then stop talking. Silence after the ask is strength. Time: 1 min + Q&A. Q&A prep: see companion document - layered answers for the 8 anticipated questions.
